position.symbolic_location: Anonymous reconstructed roof standing on the north frontage of the South Division block between Clark and Dearborn, in the party-line row at Lake and Dearborn
position.note: PARTY-LINE FRONTAGE, DERIVED FROM THE COMMITTED PLAT (T-0077). This building does not stand where a northing in the recipe put it: it stands on the north face of blk_lake_clark, whose line and bearing are read from the block boundary in data/traces/vectors/thompson_lots.json — the same committed geometry the lot grid and the corridor gate are derived from. Its front wall is set 0.80 m back from that lot line, the alignment the two frontage buildings already standing on this face use, and its east wall is fixed by the west wall of recon_1835_south_c3_015, which it shares a party line with. The bearing is the face's own, and this placement carries none of the jitter the parcel's interior rows carry, because a shared party wall is one wall and cannot wander. WHAT IS INVENTED IS STILL EVERYTHING THAT MATTERS: that a building stood here at all, which building it was, and that these particular units stood shoulder to shoulder. What the plate supports is the TREATMENT — a continuous storefront row on the town's principal street rather than detached cottages set back on grass — and the treatment is what this placement takes from it. Standing on a derived block face is not standing on a recovered lot.

occupants.note: ADOPTED BY THE INFERRED-HOUSEHOLD PROGRAMME (docs/ROADMAP.md K1, phase two). This anonymous roof is the dwelling of an inferred blacksmith's household (1 of 3 this layer infers): hh_inf_blacksmith_south_01 in data/residents/households/. THE ROOF'S OWN EXISTENCE, POSITION AND FOOTPRINT REMAIN CONJECTURAL and are unchanged by the adoption; what the adoption adds is an argued occupant instead of an anonymous count-unit. The occupant is hypothesised from the town's demonstrable needs - the 1835 census of 3,265 people in 398 dwellings against the trades Andreas's 1833 roster names - and is not a person: no name is claimed and no figure is drawn.

frontage.why: T-0077, the owner's ask of 2026-08-18 on the Tremont House street scene: "there should be more and denser buildings. this is important." He sent the plate of this corner — a continuous two-storey storefront row, shoulder to shoulder on shared party lines — beside a screenshot of this same corner in the render, where the Tremont stands alone on open grass. Four of this row's anonymous roofs stood in the Clark-Dearborn block SEVENTEEN TO TWENTY-FOUR METRES behind the Lake Street frontage, each nudged off the line by its own jitter, which is the shape of a distribution and not of a street. They now stand ON the frontage: the line, its bearing and the corner they pack back from are read from the committed block boundary in data/traces/vectors/thompson_lots.json, and this file authors no coordinate for any of them. The 0.80 m setback is not a measurement — it is the line the two frontage buildings ALREADY standing on this face (inf_bakery_lake and inf_butcher_market) use, adopted so the street wall is one wall rather than three. No roof is added, moved out of its block, renamed or re-dimensioned: the parcel still deals 40 principal and 8 ancillary, and every id and band is the one it was.
